Presentation.description: FullStack developer with {years}+ years of experience building end-to-end web applications with TypeScript, React/Next.js and Node/NestJS. I like building complete products: for GeekLog I built the website and the Android app of a social network for movies, TV shows, books and games, with a NestJS API, real-time features with Socket.IO, queues and Stripe payments. Today, at Bttis, I work on APIs, interfaces, deployment and production support.

Projects.title: Personal Projects

raioX.summary: Platform to explore the public spending of Brazilian congresspeople from official open data: parliamentary allowance, budget amendments, suppliers, rankings and side-by-side comparison.
raioX.problem: Congresspeople's spending is public, but it is scattered across different APIs and spreadsheets from the Chamber, the Senate and the Transparency Portal, which makes it hard to cross-reference. Raio-X brings it all together and shows the official source and the last sync date on every page.
highlights: Ingestion with NestJS + BullMQ: scheduled, idempotent jobs load official APIs and CSVs into PostgreSQL. The front-end never calls the government directly, so the site stays up even when the official sources are down.
Turborepo monorepo: web, API and worker share Zod schemas and the Prisma client, with strict TypeScript and ESLint without "any".
REST API documented with Swagger and Redis caching on the aggregation endpoints.
Statistical "points of attention": expenses above the 99th percentile and Q3 + 3×IQR of their category, and spending concentrated on a single supplier.
Unit tests with Vitest, API e2e tests with Supertest and front-end tests with Playwright + axe-core, all running in GitHub Actions CI.

geeklog.summary: Social network to review and share movies, TV shows, books and games with friends, with a website and an Android app.
geeklog.problem: People who consume many kinds of media end up with lists and ratings spread across several apps: one for movies, another for books, another for games. GeekLog brings everything into a single profile, with a social feed among friends.
highlights: Turborepo monorepo with three apps: a Next.js website, a NestJS (Fastify) API and an Android app built with React Native and Expo.
Real-time features with Socket.IO and background jobs with Bull queues, monitored with Bull Board.
JWT authentication, media uploads to AWS S3 with presigned URLs, payments with Stripe and emails with React Email.
MongoDB with Prisma, Redis caching and metrics exposed to Prometheus and Grafana.
Tests with Vitest and GitHub Actions CI that builds and publishes the API's Docker image.

clothShowcase.summary: 3D fitting room: from a photo of a garment, the piece is dressed on a 3D character that you can rotate and adjust right in the browser.
clothShowcase.problem: A product photo doesn't show how the garment looks on a body. The fitting room turns an ordinary photo into a 3D piece worn by the character, with nothing to install.
highlights: Photo analysis in the browser: separates the garment from the background and finds the main fabric color, the collar, the waist and whether it has sleeves.
Fitting driven by the skeleton: shoulders, collar, chest and arm angle are measured on the model itself.
The body's shape keys become controls (weight, muscle, hips) and the garment follows the deformations.
Automated 3D model pipeline with Python scripts in Blender: rig, shape keys, clothes and animation.

nftMarketplace.summary: NFT marketplace with a catalog, cart, checkout with a simulated wallet, real-time updates and user account.
nftMarketplace.problem: Front-end challenge: build the full purchase experience without a backend, while handling the problems of a real API, such as latency, outages, errors and prices changing mid-purchase.
highlights: The whole API is mocked in the browser with MSW (in-memory database persisted to localStorage), including real-time updates over Socket.IO.
Controllable failure scenarios: latency, offline mode, one-off 500 errors, refused payment and expired coupon.
Order creation with an Idempotency-Key that recovers from timeouts without duplicating the purchase.
Routing and data with TanStack Router and TanStack Query, forms with React Hook Form + Zod.
E2E tests with Playwright + axe-core and performance audits with Lighthouse.
